question: Pipe P can fill (5)/(9) part of a tank in 25 hours, and pipe Q can fill (3)/(7) part of the same tank in 27 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 3 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 4 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Full time for **P** = 25 × (9/5) = 45 hours and **Q** = 27 × (7/3) = 63 hours.

LCM of 45 and 63 is 315 units (Total Work). Efficiency: **P** = 7, **Q** = 5.

Work done in 3 hours = (7 + 5) × 3 = 36 units. Efficiency of **R** = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 (Emptying).

Net efficiency (P + Q − R) = 7 + 5 − 9 = 3 units/hr.

Time taken = 315 ÷ 3 = 105 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 105 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Pipe P fills 5/9 part in 25 hr, Pipe Q fills 3/7 part in 27 hr. R empties the filled part in 4 hr.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency; Time = Total Work ÷ Net Efficiency.

⇒ Total capacity of tank = 315 units.

⇒ Amount filled by P and Q in 3 hours = (7 + 5) × 3 = 36 units.

⇒ Pipe R empties 36 units in 4 hours.

⇒ Efficiency of R = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 units/hr (Negative as it is an outlet pipe).

⇒ Combined efficiency of P, Q, and R = 7 + 5 − 9 = 3 units/hr.

⇒ Time required to fill the tank together = 315 ÷ 3 = 105 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 105 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Inlet pipes have **positive efficiency** while outlet pipes (leaks) have **negative efficiency**.

Total Work via LCM

Always calculate the time taken to fill the **whole tank** (1 unit) before taking the LCM to find total capacity.

Work and Time Relation

If a pipe fills a tank in 'x' hours, its 1-hour work is 1/x of the total capacity.</p
